transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

I can handle the technical parts fine, but I just can’t seem to keep all the pieces of these projects organized anymore. Since my promotion to lead architect about a year ago, I'm really struggling to manage all the different moving parts and planning.
Did these organization and attention problems start only after your promotion, or have you had similar difficulties since childhood or school?

Honestly, looking back, these issues have been with me since primary school. My teachers used to write comments on my report cards like "brilliant ideas but careless mistakes," and my parents literally had to sit with me just to keep me from drifting off during simple homework. It just became a massive roadblock over the last year with the added demands of this new lead role.
Do you also often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble waiting your turn or interrupting others, or is the main problem just inattention and disorganization?

While the disorganization is my biggest hurdle, I definitely get a physical restlessness, like a "restless buzz" during long Zoom calls where I have to constantly shift in my chair or pace to burn off energy. Even with quiet hobbies like reading, I get too antsy to just sit still in silence. I don't really have issues with interrupting people or waiting my turn, though.
Do you often act impulsively, such as blurting out answers, interrupting others, making quick decisions without thinking, or spending money before you mean to?
No, I don't really struggle with impulsivity, interrupting others, or making impulsive purchases. Those behaviors don't really sound like me at all.
Do these attention and restlessness symptoms cause problems in more than one area of your life, such as at work, at home, or in social situations?

Yes, they definitely affect multiple areas of my life. At work, my disorganization has led to missed integration points, delayed deliverables, and a poor performance review that has me seriously worried about my job security. It's also spilled over into my personal and creative life, where I've started forgetting workshop commitments, gallery submissions, and travel plans.
Before age 12, did you already have these attention or restlessness problems at home or school, such as being easily distracted, forgetting homework, or fidgeting in class?

Yes, absolutely, those issues definitely go back to before I was 12. In primary school, my teachers constantly wrote "brilliant ideas but careless mistakes" on my report cards because of how easily distracted I was. At home, my parents literally had to sit right next to me just to keep me focused enough to finish simple homework without drifting off.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, predominantly inattentive presentation: longstanding symptoms since childhood, clear inattention/disorganization with careless mistakes and difficulty sustaining focus, associated restlessness, impairment across work and personal domains, and onset before age 12. Hyperactive/impulsive symptoms are limited, but the inattentive syndrome is sufficient for the diagnosis given the history and functional impact.
